newsitem.title: USA: Tenneco holders approve El Paso deal, spin-off.
newsitem.headline: Tenneco holders approve El Paso deal, spin-off.

text.p: Tenneco Inc. said Tuesday its shareholders approved the merger of Tenneco Energy with El Paso Energy Corp. and the spin-off of its Newport News Shipbuilding unit, the last step in a massive restructuring of a once unwieldy conglomerate.

Tenneco, which had operated businesses from natural gas pipelines to shipbuilding, will be left with automotive parts, packaging and administrative services businesses after the transactions, the company said.
"Today's vote is the culmination of a sustained five-year effort to turn around what was once a troubled conglomerate," said Dana Mead, Tenneco chairman and chief executive.

"We have created a 'new' Tenneco focused on our highly successful automotive parts and packaging businesses with great potential for additional value creation. During this dramatic transformation, we have generated substantial growth in earnings per share and greatly strengthened the company's balance sheet."
With the spin-offs and merger, Tenneco common shareholdes will receive one share of the new holding company for each share of current Tenneco stock.
They will also get one Newport News share for every five current Tenneco shares and one El Paso share for about every 10 current Tenneco shares.
Since late 1991, Tenneco has spun off its Case agricultural and construction equipment and Albright & Wilson chemical subsidiaries; sold its minerals business and merged the energy division.
The company has cut its debt by almost $5.5 billion, increased the dividend by 12.5 percent, and invested nearly $800 million in Tenneco common stock repurchase programmes.
Tenneco, based in Greenwich, Conn., said it expected revenues to rise to of $11.1 billion this year from $8.9 billion in 1995.
Tenneco's stock edged down 12.5 cents to $51.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in afternoon trading.
